subject: Keystone onboarding: load verification cadence & acceptance artifacts
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Oliver Park <oliver.park@keystone.ai>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 12 Mar 2028 09:15:00 -07:00
Subject: Keystone onboarding: load verification cadence & acceptance artifacts

Hi Oliver —

Great to meet you virtually last week. As discussed, we want to align on a short, pragmatic load verification cadence so your engineering team can validate throughput and tail-latency against the contract SLOs before we flip production traffic. Attached is a lightweight plan (redwood_loadplan_20280312.pdf) and our recommended acceptance matrix.

High-level ask: please confirm the three test windows below and whether Keystone can provide the test harness (API endpoint and a short sample dataset) by Wednesday EOD PT. If you prefer, we can run the harness from our side — just need short-lived API credentials.

Proposed windows (PST):
- Smoke: Thu 2028-03-15 08:00–09:00 — single-client concurrency, baseline tail-latency checks
- Ramp: Fri 2028-03-16 09:00–12:00 — step ramp to sustained concurrency target (see sheet)
- Soak/Validation: Mon 2028-03-19 01:00–05:00 — sustained traffic at target QPS for 4 hours; capture KV cache behavior

Acceptance criteria (summary):
- P50/P95/P99 latency under agreed thresholds in keystone_SLOs_v1.xlsx
- No more than 0.5% 5xx across ramp/soak phases
- No KV cache loss after warmup (> 99.5% cache hit for prefix sets)

Attachments referenced: redwood_loadplan_20280312.pdf (test schedule + tooling), sample acceptance matrix (keystone_SLOs_v1.xlsx).

Next steps: confirm windows, who from Keystone will own the harness, and whether procurement needs to be looped for a short-term test license. I’m copying Monica to coordinate instrumentation and Ben for any contractual notes.

Thanks,
Marissa
Marissa Cole
Senior Customer Success Manager
Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0148

---
Attachment stubs: redwood_loadplan_20280312.pdf (application/pdf), keystone_SLOs_v1.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet)

From: Oliver Park <oliver.park@keystone.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Keystone Technical Team <tech@keystone.ai>, Maya Singh <maya.singh@keystone.ai>
Date: Mon, 12 Mar 2028 12:45:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Keystone onboarding: load verification cadence & acceptance artifacts

Marissa —

Thanks for the clear plan. This looks good from a high level. Our infra lead (Maya) will own the harness and can deliver a zipped harness and a small synthetic dataset by Wednesday midday PT. I’ve attached a short tech note and the current SLO draft (we made one small change to the P99 target, which I’ve highlighted).

We can commit to the proposed windows, with one ask: can the ramp window be split into two shorter ramps (09:00–10:30 and 10:45–12:00) so we can sanity-check autoscaling behavior between steps? If so, we’ll run both and provide server-side telemetry (CPU, GPU, network) and a basic tracing dump.

Also looping procurement@keystone.ai (cc’d internally) — they may need an internal PO to enable the test license.

Oliver Park
Head of Platform Engineering, Keystone.ai
oliver.park@keystone.ai
+1 (617) 555-0102

---
Attachment stubs: keystone_test_harness.zip (application/zip), keystone_SLOs_v1.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Oliver Park <oliver.park@keystone.ai>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 13 Mar 2028 08:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Keystone onboarding: load verification cadence & acceptance artifacts

Thanks Oliver — confirmed on our side. Splitting the ramp into two windows is fine; we’ll reflect that in the revised schedule.

Quick clarifications before we lock times:
1) Ramp targets: we need the exact QPS/concurrency numbers you intend to hit for each step. Please put them in the harness README or reply inline.
2) API credentials: short-lived API key with telemetry access (read-only) is preferred. If you’d rather hand us the harness and run from Keystone, we can do that too — let us know preference.
3) Data sensitivity: if the dataset contains PII, we’ll need a data-processing addendum signed; otherwise, synthetic is fine.

Monica — action for you: can you prepare the instrumentation checklist (tracing config, tokenization debug flags, and the telemetry dashboard link) and share a short runbook by Wednesday? Ben — flag any contract/credit concerns for the test license.

I’m attaching an updated schedule PDF (redwood_loadplan_20280312.pdf) with the ramp split and a short internal runbook excerpt.

Best,
Marissa

Attachment stubs: redwood_loadplan_20280312.pdf (application/pdf)

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Oliver Park <oliver.park@keystone.ai>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 13 Mar 2028 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Keystone onboarding: load verification cadence & acceptance artifacts

Quick note from procurement/sales side: we can provide a short-term test license for the three windows — no charge aside from standard usage — but I need confirmation by EOD Wednesday so we can route the internal approval. If Keystone wants usage credits instead of direct testing on our infra, we can structure that too (HubSpot deal notes updated).

Also, do we want to include a small canary at 10% production traffic after the soak run (Mon 2028-03-19 08:00–09:00 PT)? That would give Keystone an extra safety step before full cutover.

Ben
Ben Carter
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.ai

Quoted for context:
> On Tue, Mar 13, 2028 at 08:30 AM Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai> wrote:
> > Monica — action for you: can you prepare the instrumentation checklist...

From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Oliver Park <oliver.park@keystone.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 14 Mar 2028 16:00:00 -07:00
Subject: Keystone onboarding: runbook, telemetry, and acceptance summary

Hi all —

Thanks for the quick turnaround. A few operational notes and confirmed artifacts so everyone has a single source of truth before tests begin: 

1) What Redwood will provide (attached and in Drive):
- Instrumentation checklist (tracing, Prometheus exporters, and tag mappings)
- Runbook: steps to start/stop traffic, how to toggle KV cache warmup, and a post-run evidence checklist
- Evidence template: sample CSV to capture request-level latency, status codes, and trace ids

2) What Keystone will provide:
- Test harness (keystone_test_harness.zip) + README with explicit QPS/concurrency targets for each ramp step
- Short-lived API key with read-only telemetry access OR a contact to run harness on your side (Maya)
- Host-level metrics (GPU utilization, memory, net) for ramp/soak windows

3) Acceptance gating (final):
- P50 < 60ms, P95 < 180ms, P99 < 600ms (see keystone_SLOs_v1.xlsx for full matrix)
- Sustained error rate < 0.5% across ramp/soak, and no degradation during canary at 10% prod traffic
- Evidence: request CSV, Grafana dashboard snapshot, and a short written sign-off from Keystone eng lead

4) Schedule recap (PT):
- Smoke: 2028-03-15 08:00–09:00
- Ramp A: 2028-03-16 09:00–10:30
- Ramp B: 2028-03-16 10:45–12:00
- Soak/Validation: 2028-03-19 01:00–05:00
- Optional Canary: 2028-03-19 08:00–09:00

Please drop the harness README into the shared Drive link (https://drive.redwood.com/drive/folders/onboard-keystone-2028) and reply to this thread once the API key or run contact is available. Ben — confirm the test license routing and I’ll add the final runbook to the HubSpot deal.

Monica Patel
Implementation Lead, Customer Success
Redwood Inference
monica.patel@redwood.ai
